content:
sam: Quick flag — dev noticed some high-cardinality identifiers showing up in sampled request/response logs for embeddings/reranker pipelines. What should our canonical policy be for sampling vs redaction? :thinking:

kevin: Short answer: redact before storage whenever possible. Longer: sampling should happen at collection time, but we still need per-route exceptions for debugging. Hashing IDs is ok for routing, but not enough for storage if entropy is low. Prefer salted hashing + bucket checks.

kevin: Example config we use in staging (pseudo):
```
sampling:
  mode: per_route
  default_rate: 0.02
  pii_protect: true
  hash_salt: env(PII_SALT)
  min_bucket_size: 20
```

anya: UX note — console needs a clear, auditable "inspect" toggle per-route. It should be off by default, show the reason it was enabled, and require breakglass approval for >1h. Also show estimated PII exposure (percent of samples marked sensitive). :lock: @kevin

jordan: For metrics/SLAs: we should keep token counts, latency, and cost per-sample but strip content. If teams need a sample payload for QA, send to an encrypted, TTL'd bucket and require an audit log entry. That keeps observability but reduces blast radius.

kevin: Agreed. Add automatic TTL of 30d for any retained payloads and store only metadata (route, hashed_user, truncated_prompt) in main telemetry. Move vectors/embeddings to an encrypted store with separate ACLs.

sam: How do we handle quota/routing implications? Some routes have low volume but high PII rate; sampling them at 2% could miss patterns.

anya: Per-route override: allow higher sample rate for labeled-safe routes, but add a circuit breaker that disables payload retention if >0.5% of recent samples flagged as sensitive. Display circuit state in console.

kevin: Implementation note: add a fast path in the router that marks payloads for `ephemeral-inspect` vs `hashed-metadata`. Ephemeral goes to inspect pipeline (short TTL, stricter ACLs). Hashed-metadata goes to analytics. Also log an event when circuit trips: `inspect.disabled.reason=high_sensitive_rate`.

infra-bot: logs-forwarder: paused pipeline "inspect-forward" at 2350012370 after retention-policy mismatch. See: https://internal.redwood/logs/inspect-forward/2350012370 :eyes:

sam: OK — proposed rollout: canary at 1% routes for 24h, then 10% for 48h, then full. Add automatic rollback if circuit trips or if any PII leak alert firing. @kevin @anya please confirm deploy checklist.

kevin: Confirm. I'll add the salt rotation step and unit tests for min_bucket_size. Also add a console banner when inspect is enabled.

anya: Confirm. I'll draft the UX copy and the audit trail schema. Suggest label: "Inspect (PII-guarded) — requires audit and SSO group approval".

jordan: I'll add SLOs to monitor lost observability (alerts when sampling reduces signal on top routes) so teams can request exceptions via support flow.

sam: Thanks. Next steps: kevin -> infra PR for router flags, anya -> console mockups, jordan -> SLO/alerts doc. Will follow up in #eng-platform-sync tomorrow. :thumbsup:
